findings.title: Proposition 6.7 includes the trivial group
findings.claim: For every connected commutative affine algebraic subgroup G of Bir(X), rRepl_X(G) is self-centralizing; G is not required to be nontrivial.
assumptions_verified: k=C is algebraically closed, uncountable and characteristic zero.
G={id} is a closed connected commutative affine algebraic subgroup; its inclusion is faithful.

check.calculation: Rat^G(X,G) has one element, hence rRepl_X(G)={id}; Cent_Bir(X)({id})=Bir(X), and z->z+1 is a nonidentity centralizing element.
check.result: The equality in Proposition 6.7 fails under its literal hypotheses.

counterevidence: No general nontrivial-subgroup convention was found; Theorem 6.1 adds nontriviality explicitly.
Main uses take positive-dimensional additive/vector groups or tori; the counterexample does not occur there.
findings.core_dependency: Proposition 6.7 supports Theorems 1.1 and 1.2, but the defective trivial input is excluded by their actual constructions.

correction.verification: The missing boundary is excluded and generic orbit group G' is nontrivial, permitting point-separating rational maps in Claim 3. Full imported quotient machinery not re-proved.

findings.title: Irreducible branch polynomial cannot be chosen at n=2
findings.claim: For the construction of Corollary 1.4, choose homogeneous irreducible degree-2n F in k[x0,...,x_{n-1}], with n>=2.
assumptions_verified: n=2 is included in the corollary.
k is algebraically closed of characteristic zero.

check.type: analytic factorization and explicit corrected geometry
check.calculation: Every binary quartic factors into four linear forms over k. Replacement F=x1*(x1-x0)*(x1-2*x0)*(x1-3*x0) has four distinct branch points; f=y(y-1)(y-2)(y-3) has valuation 1 at y=0 and is nonsquare. The smooth completed double cover has 2g-2=-4+4=0. The T_f matrices are invertible because a^2-b^2*f cannot vanish for nonzero (a,b).
check.result: The original irreducibility condition is impossible at n=2; the explicit squarefree replacement preserves the needed nonsquare/non-ruled properties.

counterevidence: The paper cites reference [20] for the already proved n=2 case; an intended restriction of the new construction to n>=3 is a valid alternative resolution.
This does not refute the corollary or the higher-dimensional construction.
findings.core_dependency: Only the already-known two-dimensional endpoint of the construction is affected, with no demonstrated damage to the principal new rationality results.

correction.statement: At n=2 use a squarefree binary quartic as above, or explicitly restrict this new construction to n>=3 and invoke the cited n=2 result.
correction.verification: Explicit replacement checked analytically; the cited external proof was not independently audited.

independent_acceptance_check.scope: Independent recheck of both existing boundary findings, exact definitions and standing characteristic-zero assumptions, principal application exclusions and explicit repairs; publisher Version of Record only.
independent_acceptance_check.disposition: Retain both Minor findings; the demonstrated bad inputs do not invalidate the checked principal applications.
independent_acceptance_check.P1: For X=P1 over C and faithful inclusion G={1}, Definition 6.5 gives exactly one replica, the identity. Its centralizer is all Bir(P1), containing z->z+1. Proposition 6.7 has no nontriviality restriction, and Claim 3 fails at the demanded point-separating map into G'. Adding G!=1 removes the concrete boundary and ensures positive-dimensional generic orbit; it does not reprove the imported quotient machinery.
independent_acceptance_check.P1_counterevidence: Theorem 1.1 uses U with replica group containing the nontrivial translation image, so U and the corresponding torus are nontrivial. Theorem 1.2 explicitly uses Ga and Gm. The counterexample lies outside these actual applications.
independent_acceptance_check.P2: Over an algebraically closed field an irreducible binary quartic cannot exist. The squarefree replacement x1*(x1-x0)*(x1-2x0)*(x1-3x0) has four simple finite branch points, is nonsquare by valuation one, and gives a genus-one non-ruled double cover by Riemann-Hurwitz. The matrix determinant a^2-b^2*f stays nonzero for (a,b)!=0, and x0 is not a factor.
independent_acceptance_check.P2_counterevidence: The introduction expressly identifies n=2 as already proved in reference [20]. Restricting the new construction to n>=3 and using that cited case is another limited resolution; the external proof was not audited. The finding concerns presentation of that endpoint, not a failure of the new principal rationality results.
independent_acceptance_check.consistency: Report and both findings preserve exact source locations, limited repairs, counterevidence and bounded coverage; no whole-paper certification.
